description: 24x24 Japanese ideographs missed by the CJK-only OCR acceptance rule because their bitmaps were recognized as kana, symbols, or ASCII-like forms. This file is an additive audit result and does not modify manual_glyph_evidence.json.
key_policy: Each sha256_prefix is a unique prefix of the raw 24x24 glyph bitmap SHA-256 in unique_24px_glyphs.csv.

method: atlas bitmap inspection in union-index order
Windows Japanese OCR and MS Gothic template comparison
local font slot to extracted-message context tracing
cross-check against numbered-book series and repeated dialogue contexts

entries.evidence: Square glyph is the 口/ロ homograph. Message contexts independently require 口: 差込口1/2, 端麗辛口, 超辛口, 一口大, 口の中, and 口に広がる. MS Gothic template top-1 is 口 (0.80720079).
Two-stroke 二/ニ homograph. Repeated message contexts require 二, including 二本一組, 二足歩行, 二見すると, 二度, and 二段技. MS Gothic template top-1 is 二 (0.92432106), ahead of 工 (0.89575368).
夕/タ homograph. Seven extracted occurrences form the fixed phrase 夕暮れの半刻. MS Gothic template top-1 is 夕 (0.87467414).
Two-stroke 二/ニ homograph. The extracted sentence requires 二酸化硫黄物語. MS Gothic template top-1 is 二 (0.92432106), ahead of 工 (0.89575368).
夕/タ homograph. Extracted contexts require 明日の夕方 and 夕暮れの半刻. MS Gothic template top-1 is 夕 (0.87467414).
Japanese ideographic zero is outside the merge script's unified-ideograph class. All six extracted uses are the date placeholder 〇月×日, and all three Windows OCR variants unanimously recognize 〇.

Horizontal 一/ー homograph. Its four-glyph message is 一の書～. The same numbered-book series contains 二の書～, 三の書～, 五の書～, 六の書～, and 七の書～ in sibling font containers. MS Gothic template top-1 is 一 (0.72400028).
Stylized 二/ニ homograph. Its four-glyph message is 二の書～, confirmed by the sibling numbered-book messages 一の書～, 三の書～, 五の書～, 六の書～, and 七の書～.
力/カ homograph. The fully reconstructed riddle sentence reads 内に秘めたる力を解き放つは何者ぞ, which uniquely establishes 力 rather than katakana カ.

false_positive_recheck.evidence_summary: Atlas inspection and message reconstruction reconfirm these as Greek alpha/beta, Latin letters or digits, solid/block UI marks, a circled digit, section/hash-like marks, or tiny stylized non-kanji lettering. Examples include U0451 in セクターα〔セクターアルファ〕, U08A9 as a Latin A, U08AD as a Latin V, U08C5 as a solid UI delimiter around 工房設備, U0EC6 as circled 3, U113C as #, and U1264 as digit 2.

excluded_correct_non_kanji_examples.reason: Correct Japanese iteration mark, not a kanji ideograph; observed in 回々, 山々, 代々, 色々, and 我々 contexts.
Horizontal homograph is a katakana prolonged-sound mark in フォーテ…, エクスキューショナー, and related katakana contexts, not 一.
Used inside the katakana rendering of デバイス, not 八.
Used as lowercase Latin l in PlayStation, not 一 or a vertical CJK stroke.
Used in エンカウンター, not 力.
Used in エンカウンター, not 夕.
Used in ドルビーデジタルプロロジックⅡ, not a kanji.
Used in the Latin abbreviation vol.3, not 丨 or 一.
